newsitem.title: GREECE: Construction, industrials prop Greek stocks higher.
newsitem.headline: Construction, industrials prop Greek stocks higher.

text.p: Late buying helped Greek shares come out of their lethargy and finish 0.21 percent higher on Thursday with a rise in construction and industrials offsetting a drift in banks.

Trading wound down ahead of the long weekend. The Athens bourse will be closed on Friday August 15 in observation of the Assumption of the Virgin. The next trading session will be staged on Monday August 18.

"Greek equities are hovering above 1,600 points awaiting for news on the 1998 Budget and broader fiscal policy as well as the outcome of Athens' bid for hosting the 2004 Olympics," said Vasilios Kletsas, broker at Telesis Securities.
"Should Athens be given the green light, I expect Greek equities to appreciate on sentiment," he added.

Athens along with Rome are the favourites for the selection, with Stockholm, Cape Town and Buenos Aires being the outsiders. An announcement for the host city for the Games is expected on September 5.
Prime minister Costats Simitis is expected to outline next year's economic policy at his opening speach at the Thessaloniki international trade fair in early September.

"The market has held on to its earlier gains despite a halt in the improvement of macroeconomic indicators, including fiscal revenues growth, CPI inflation and the current account, because the outlook on a medium- to long-term horizon remains positive," Kletsas said.
Foreign portfolios continue to show interest in Greek equities, helped by a stronger dollar, but they are very selective among blue chips only, he added.
The Athens benchmark index closed 0.21 percent or 3.45 points higher at 1,645.81 from Wednesday's 1,642.36 close, trading very narrowly between 1,642.38 and 1,647.58.
Construction firmed 0.93 percent, closely followed by industrials which added 0.92 percent, propped by a 3.23 percent climb in Hellenic Bottling. Banks closed 0.17 percent lower.

Turnover was 8.3 billion drachmas on volume of 2.2 million shares, helped by block trading in a number of blue chips, including Alpha Credit, around 28,000 shares at 20,170 drachmas, OTE telecom, 60,000 shares at 6,500, Ergobank, 11,392 shares at 17,990, and Titan Cement, 20,000 shares at 15,220.
Advancers outpaced decliners 107 to 93 with 35 shares unchanged on 235 traded.
OTE telecom OTEq.L Global Depository Shares (GDS) were quoted on London's SEAQ International market at $11.1-$11.5. Two GDSs make up one share of OTE.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas, capped at 5,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,129-1,159 drachmas.

The recently launched second Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 6,800 drachmas, capped at 10,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,113-1,173 drachmas. The warrants expire December 16, 1998. Shares of the underlying stock lost 25 drachmas to 6,550.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 693.55-737.82 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $76.90-$79.75. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 3,999-4,230 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $12.34 bid/no offer. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 244-276 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998.
